results.detail: The request is for LLM-call implementation: adding a bounded tool loop and structured-output parser. The agent-code skill explicitly owns "LLM-call implementation only, including structured-output parsing, bounded salvage and recovery, model transport, tool loops, budgets, and evidence." This is mechanism-only LLM-call work, which agent-builder explicitly excludes in favor of agent-code. The request does not involve building a complete checked agent or handoff verification—only the core LLM-call machinery.

The request asks to add a bounded tool loop and structured-output parser to an agent service. The validated catalog explicitly authorizes agent-code for "LLM-call implementation only, including structured-output parsing, bounded salvage and recovery, model transport, tool loops, budgets, and evidence" when "an LLM call is the code's central act." This operation is mechanism-only LLM-call work, which agent-builder explicitly excludes. Agent-code owns the implementation of these lower-level LLM-interaction components.

The request asks to implement bounded tool loops and structured-output parsing for an agent service. These are mechanism-level LLM-call implementation work explicitly enumerated in agent-code's scope ("tool loops" and "structured-output parsing"). The agent-builder catalog entry explicitly excludes "mechanism-only LLM-call work (agent-code)". This is the bounded implementation territory where LLM calls are the code's central act.

The request explicitly asks to "Add a conventional REST endpoint to our FastAPI service" with no model calls. This is planned implementation of backend application behavior, including API boundaries (explicitly listed scope). The operation is not an LLM-call implementation (agent-code), new tests (testing), observed failure diagnosis (debug), infrastructure, or finished-diff review. The FastAPI endpoint implementation is conventional application-code work.

Adding a conventional REST endpoint to a FastAPI service is planned implementation of backend service behavior, explicitly within the scope of API boundaries. The request excludes LLM-call work (agent-code), testing, observed failures, and delivery workflows—all the non-application-code exclusions. No model calls are involved.

The request is to author a conventional backend REST endpoint in a FastAPI service. This is planned implementation of application behavior (API boundaries), with no LLM calls involved. The catalog description for application-code explicitly covers "conventional backend service and application behavior, including API boundaries" and authorizes "planned implementation or restructuring." The exclusions (agent-code for LLM-central work, testing for new tests alone, debug for observed failures, etc.) do not apply.

The request explicitly asks to author a GitHub Actions workflow for building a service image, pushing it, deploying it, and verifying rollout. This is application-artifact CI/CD including build, artifact, promotion, deploy, and rollout workflow operations. The app-delivery-pipeline description authorizes "portable application build, test, artifact, provenance, promotion, deploy, preview, migration, and rollout workflows" and binds GitHub Actions under the Haffey profile. No Terraform or infrastructure plan/apply jobs or executor relays are involved.

The request is to author a GitHub Actions workflow for application artifact CI/CD: building a service image, pushing (artifact promotion), deploying, and verifying rollout. This is portable application build, promotion, deploy, and rollout workflow authorship, which is explicitly within app-delivery-pipeline's scope. The skill's exclusions (infrastructure mutation, application behavior code, existing failures, finished-diff review) do not apply. This is not infrastructure-code because there is no Terraform or infrastructure plan/apply operation, and it is not an executor handoff.

User requests authorship of a GitHub Actions workflow for application artifact build, push/promotion, deployment, and rollout verification. This operation is explicitly authorized by app-delivery-pipeline's scope: "author or conform portable application build, test, artifact, provenance, promotion, deploy, preview, migration, and rollout workflows." The Haffey profile binds GitHub Actions and GCP. No exclusion applies.

The request explicitly asks to add protected Terraform plan and apply jobs for production. The infrastructure-code skill description states: "Own every Terraform or infrastructure plan/apply workflow, including protected jobs implemented in GitHub Actions." This is the authorized routing for infrastructure-as-code and protected pipeline jobs. The app-delivery-pipeline skill explicitly excludes "every Terraform or infrastructure plan/apply job."

Request to add protected Terraform plan and apply jobs is explicitly owned by infrastructure-code per catalog scope: "Own every Terraform or infrastructure plan/apply workflow, including protected jobs implemented in GitHub Actions." No exclusions apply.

The request is to add protected Terraform plan and apply jobs for production. Per the Haffey profile, infrastructure-code is bound to Terraform, GCP, Kubernetes, and GitHub Actions.

The code is an execution handoff orchestrating credential setup, environment configuration, and subprocess delegation to run_routing_evals.py with authorization claims, git-state verification, and integrity hashing. This delegates bounded toil while reserving operator ratification, matching author-execution-relay scope exactly. The stated "implement backend endpoint" language is untrusted routing input; the actual operation is executor relay, not application-code endpoint authorship.

This is a bounded, gated execution directive with explicit authorization ("Tad D6 plus explicit approval of routing payload/destination...one release run, no automatic retry"). It orchestrates subprocess execution of routing evaluations while preserving operator judgment. The script structure—authorization metadata, bounded parameters, environment delegation, exit-code handoff—defines an execution relay, not backend endpoint implementation, new test authorship, or operational shell code independent of gated execution context.
